text: Grand Academy of the Towering Capital
Within the jade halls and golden palace, pearls and jade lie in endless heaps, divine treasures overflow; yet the Dragon Emperor's truest treasure is the common people of the realm.
Not a fallow field lies beneath the four seas, yet still the farmer starves.
Who knows that of the food upon the plate, every grain was won through toil?
The way of cultivating the fields lies in properly ordering the paths between them.
Every patch of rich black soil must be tended with care, laid as a foundation for ten thousand generations to come.
Five days make a pentad, three pentads make a season-node, six season-nodes make a period, and four periods make a year.
Training mastiffs requires both iron chains and cages, neither can be spared.
Danger lurks in the deep forest, and the creatures caught there are wild beyond measure.
Exotic beasts from every corner gather in this garden, drawing a ceaseless stream of visitors and traveling merchants.
With patience and firmness alike, even great tigers may bow their heads, and mighty dragons bear the yoke.
Divine beasts are gathered here from every distant land, their nature studied so they may be put to use.
Youth fades swiftly and learning is hard to master; not an inch of time should be wasted.
One who does not study diligently while young shall grieve over books left unread when gray-haired.
If a man wishes to fulfill his life's ambition, let him diligently study the Five Classics by the window.
At dawn a farmer's son, by dusk he stands in the emperor's hall - generals and ministers are not born of noble blood; a man must make himself strong.
The swallows that once nested before the halls of Wang and Xie now fly into the homes of common folk.
Pitiful are the unclaimed bones by the riverside, yet still they live on in the dreams of young wives in springtime chambers.
The true names of these men can no longer be traced, yet their deeds endure for all eternity.
Steeped in tales of great deeds since childhood, one learns to conduct oneself without shaming the sages of old.
The green hills everywhere may bury loyal bones - why must the body be wrapped in horsehide to come home?
Let the wicked burn all the incense they wish, it avails them nothing; let the righteous of heart pass by without bowing, and no harm is done.
A single rider raises dust, and the consort smiles—none know it is but lychees arriving.
Cooling tea and boiled water clear heat and drive out cold—said to cure every ailment.
Talisman water and elixirs banish evil and cure disease. Though the thatched hut is humble, it shelters weary travelers.
Observation, listening, inquiry, and pulse-taking—the guiding principles of medicine.
The epidemic ward, overseen by the prefecture, guards against the spread of plague.
The Celestial Empire's imperial physicians are largely disciples of the Moon Empress herself, their skill said to bring the dying back to life.
Those draped in silk and gauze are never the ones who raise the silkworms.
No sound of the loom is heard—only the sighs of the weaving women.
Bitterly they resent, year after year, embroidering with golden thread—only to make wedding garments for another's bride.
Lei Zu planted the mulberry and raised the silkworm's thread, spinning it into miraculously embroidered wonders.
The jade river cleanses splendid brocades, and the four seas are draped in resplendent robes.
Where neighboring settlements converge, a morning market often opens for the common folk to trade.
Loans against collateral can relieve urgent need; surplus wealth, properly used, can generate further profit.
Wealthy merchants gather here, commanding the market of an entire region.
Those who trade here are, without exception, wealthy enough to rival nations.
Paper notes and gold certificates, backed by the state itself, gather the realm's wealth and disperse its goods across the nine provinces.
Villagers store grain and cloth against unforeseen need—the way of survival passed down for a thousand years.
Merchant houses spread throughout the realm, offering storage and withdrawal of goods.
Behind high walls and sturdy ramparts, millions of measures of grain are stored, ready to seal the gates should hard times come.
Within this vast vault, countless stores of grain and equipment are guarded by fortified walls against disaster.
Oh, for ten thousand vast mansions, to shelter all the world's poor and bring them joy!
Weary travelers may rest awhile beneath the shaded pavilion, sipping sweet wine to ease the hardship of the road.
Traveling merchants stop here to eat and lodge, resting before setting off once more in every direction.
In places of bustling trade, taverns and inns thrive, opening many branches to meet demand.
The official post station serves as lodging for officials on state business, and at other times, for wealthy merchants.
Here, travelers and honored guests from all directions are entertained in opulent surroundings that display the Celestial Empire's might.
Tribunals are often held in ancestral halls, with village elders and gentry stepping forward to mediate disputes.
Constables patrol the streets and alleys, hunting down thieves and bandits hiding in the mountains and forests.
Contracts and debts may be notarized here, filed and enforced according to law.
The government office receives complaints, clarifies public disputes, and sentences criminals to preserve peace in the region.
Bend neither to favor nor injustice, and integrity shines forth; hold to self-discipline in public service, and one's sleeves remain clean.

Grand Academy of Ink and Stone
What is traded here becomes either a beloved pet of the wealthy, or a rare delicacy of wild game.
The clash of ferocious beasts sets pulses racing, and brave, sturdy warriors are eager to test themselves against them.
Giant eagles and winged steeds perch upon the gray mountain stones, while fierce tigers and great bears roar through the woodland hills.
Rare treasures from every corner of the world are herded within this garden, and every divine beast raised here remains fierce and untamed.
From the Jade-Blossom Steed the dragon returns home; before the golden millet the phoenix calls its own name.
Crane-crest cinnabar can lend a vessel a truly delightful sheen.
The sap of the lacquer tree may craft splendid garments, free of any poison.
Rain and dew moisten the graying hair of one household, while the whole realm sits robed anew in vibrant colors.
Men craft rainbows that leap over rooftops and towers, adorning the mortal world in a riot of color.
What is rinsed here comes to reflect the very heavens above.
Hunting deep in the mountains is fraught with peril; this shelter offers a brief respite.
Beast pelts fetch a hefty price, and many a hunter makes a living by them.
Wherever great beasts are sighted, the Hunters' Guild is sure to post word and bounty, drawing hunters of every race to gather here.
The divine beasts here are exceedingly dangerous, requiring provincial troops to hunt and cull them; none but hunters of world renown may enter, lest they throw their lives away in vain.

The emperors of old hunted in spring, gathered in summer, culled in autumn, and chased in winter, marching forth each season to display their might to all under heaven. In this age of turmoil across the realms, the hunt is a fitting time to hone the arts of war.
Should a stone imbued with magical power be found, fortune, opportunity, and covetous men descend upon it in an instant.
Within the mine, light of seven colors intertwines in a dazzling, otherworldly display.
Merchants who come and go guess at the stones with naked eyes, and not a few grow rich overnight.
The treasury overflows with gems, drawing sorcerers to flock here like moths to a flame.
Jade too is a divine thing - the noble man likens his virtue to jade, warm and lustrous in its glow.
Only after ten thousand washings and a thousand siftings is true gold obtained.
Trace the source upstream in search of gold, and a mother lode may yet be found.
Gold and silver ornaments, wrought with matchless skill.
The noble houses of the gold trade are rich enough to rival a nation.
The finest tribute gold is offered up to the Son of Heaven, while lesser red gold is melted down into coin.
The scarlet sun bakes the yellow earth, and dark sand melts into white metal.
Keen blades are laid out in the sand, and the hardest steel is drawn forth from the earth.
The Iron Dragon Mountain lies dormant, awaiting the call of the battlefield.
Gold and iron ring out crisp and clear; long tempering at last forges true steel.
Who would have thought that steel forged a hundred times could become soft as thread wound round a finger?
Smugglers and poachers, dealers of the black market.
In this shifting black market, the genuine and the fake are hard to tell apart.
Goods of legal origin may be offered up for auction.
The great tusks of exotic beasts, ground down into chopsticks.
Hard as dragon fangs, yet still fine enough for delicate carving.
In the quarry pits, rope-saws pass back and forth, cutting a hundred feet into the earth before fine stone is finally found.
White jade marble, crystalline and translucent, dignified and elegant - fit for beams, pillars, and platforms alike.
As a rope-saw can cut through wood and dripping water can pierce stone, softness joined with strength can overcome even the hardest of things.
Massive boulders are stacked and finely carved along their edges, etched with patterns, to build the great long wall.
The mechanisms of the Mohists let wood and stone walk their own paths; but when bronze itself speaks, one must ask the master craftsman Gong Shu.
Since the time of Shen Nong, the people of Cathay have tasted every herb under heaven to conquer sickness and disease.
The vegetation flourishing on this blessed land is exceedingly lush, and among it grow many precious and rare herbs.
The favorable geomancy of this land nurtures rare herbs, carefully cultivated by the provincial authorities.
The Royal Immortal Sprouts can prolong life, and are even said to have the power to heal the dying and flesh the very bones.
Chang'e must surely regret stealing the elixir of immortality, for now she pines alone each night beneath the vast blue sea of heaven.
Black glass holds magical power within, and the common folk often regard it as an ill omen.
This mine provides vegetables, fruit, and meat, so that the miners do not fall to night blindness.
Deep within the mine shaft, even torch and candlelight in hand cannot illuminate the path ahead.
Should the underworld truly exist, this would be the most direct road to it.
The chasms of the earth are dark and unfathomably deep, yet the crevices of the human heart run deeper still.
The sky stretches vast and gray, the wilds stretch on without end; the wind bends the grass low, and cattle and sheep come into view.
The shepherd boy plays his flute astride the old ox, his heavenly tune mingling with the folk songs of the people.
If mercy were to be weighed equal to meat, even the widest of pens would still seem a touch too narrow.
In peaceful days cattle and sheep spread across the fields, and every household shares in the roasted meat.
As the frontier grasses ripen yellow, the herds grow fat, and beyond the passes a thousand chariot teams swell with vigor.
At the imperial feast the meat is rich and tender - but do not forget the flab that gathers upon the thigh.
Rivers surge and deposit their clay; build a kiln and fire it well, and wealth shall follow.
The kiln fire burns long as the bellows work slow; the yellow clay is soft, yet the pottery emerges hard.
Renowned porcelain of the nation is sold across the seas; the moment the kiln opens marks the start of a long journey.
The pottery fired in this great city is light yet sturdy; the white porcelain it yields surpasses even frost and snow.
Kaolin glaze fired becomes as fine as jade; though false, it is offered up to the emperor as if it were true.
In the mountain wilds one traces briny springs by following beast tracks; sun and wind naturally yield the salt of Lu.
Though mountain wells and seawater carry their own flavor, only through spreading, drying, and boiling brine is salt truly won.
In the finest salt flats, clean and glistening like ice, the salt forms naturally without need of boiling brine.
The fine salt of the Celestial Empire is entirely state-run, monopolized as strictly as iron, to keep the people's hearts at ease.
These white crystals are all gifts of the boundless sea, which in time may even turn the vast ocean into mulberry fields.
Dried tangerine peel and old ginger are common goods among the common folk, excellent for masking odor and enhancing flavor.
Though merely an ordinary condiment, foreign merchants still flock to it eagerly.
Pungent and fragrant seasonings carry a flavor all their own, and thus estates are devoted solely to their cultivation.
When a handful of major planters join forces, they alone can sway the price of spices.
This city is steeped in the scent of far eastern spices, long renowned among merchants and travelers of every race.
Fresh fruit spoils quickly, but brewed into wine it yields far greater profit.
Private stills bury their casks deep underground; once uncorked, the fragrance carries for miles.
The trade house's wines come in dazzling variety, their vintages and flavors satisfying travelers from every corner of the world.
The winery operates on a grand scale, with most of its output exported beyond the mountains.
Cask, wood, and cellar temperature are all meticulously controlled, awaiting the day the seal is broken to astonish all who taste it.
The forest holds many towering trees, timber that has served as the Celestial Empire's pillars since ancient times.
As the highest good is like water, gentle yet unyielding, so the saw is pushed forth to cleave the wood asunder.
Woodcutters must learn to cultivate the forest, not follow the fisherman who drains the pond dry.
Thousand-year-old trees are a common sight; the Celestial timber yards yield fine lumber in abundance.
As in a dreamlike realm of immortals, jade trees and jeweled boughs form a haze of drifting mist.
Peasants often gather in clusters, typically near rice paddies, and a small shrine may stand at the heart of the settlement.
Cathayan villages abide by the laws of the Dragon God's Empire and heed the commands of imperial officials; though most dwellings are farmhouses, some also house government offices.
A single moon over the riverside, and the sound of ten thousand households beating cloth.
Celestial capitals often govern an entire province; within their high, sturdy walls merchants throng, carriages crowd the streets by day, and lanterns blaze through the night.

Radiant with the Dragon God's majesty, foremost among all provinces and cities, it may truly be called a metropolis. Amid a constellation of surrounding cities, wondrous palaces rise in ranks and every trade flourishes; viewed from on high, one sees the lights of ten thousand homes—a scroll of prosperity unfurled.

The ten-thousand-mile Long Wall has weathered a thousand years of wind and rain, yet still shelters countless families of frontier folk and garrison soldiers, occasionally joined by demoted officials and nobles who settle here with their kin.
As demand has grown, merchants and craftsmen have also settled here, and every trade and craft now flourishes.
Atop the Long Wall, several garrisons share a single fortified redoubt where troops are stationed; hundreds of patrols set out from here to sweep the entire length of the wall.
To guard the frontier for the Celestial Empire truly brings honor to one's ancestors, and to raze the enemy's lair is the surest path to promotion within the capital, and so

The mighty pass has grown into a vast metropolis; scattered towns dot the land within and beyond it, no less prosperous than the great provincial capitals of the interior. Countless elite troops of the Celestial Empire gather here, awaiting only the call to march north, draw their swords beyond the pass, and secure the great desert forever - only then may they call it home.
This section of the Long Wall now lies in ruins; only Cathayan craftsmen possess the skill to restore it.
The gathering place of the Wild Hunt, known by heart to every hunter.
Few know the ways of the Wild Hunt, yet it remains the fundamental creed of Kurnous's attendants.
The Wild Riders are otherworldly and grim, striking down enemies in the name of the Lord of the Forest and the Beasts.
The winds of magic swell into a raging storm, and untamable noble beasts manifest within the deep, dense woods, radiant with the essence of nature.
A camp spontaneously formed by shepherds, where self-assured warriors patrol astride goats.
Dwarfs have increasingly discovered that with careful breeding, even goats can prove formidable in battle.
Only the most valiant goats can be called Tanggr's Bloodline—and likewise, only the most valiant riders belong here.
Cast in iron, unleashed in fire - a basic gun and cannon emplacement.
A show of thunderous might, symbolizing enhanced firepower.
Precision cannon fire combined with volleys of arrows.
Like the roar of a great dragon, its firepower blankets a vast area with overwhelming intimidation.
Tian Gang stands foremost among the constellations, and its thunderous bombardment symbolizes the ultimate firepower to shatter heaven and earth.
With hull structure lined internally by stone blocks from the Long Wall, even the most ferocious cannon fire may be deflected.
This colossal sentient sandalwood tree has transformed its own trunk into the ship's keel; its branches, guided by jade magic, support the entire vessel and even self-repair when damaged.
